good: Easy pace, just enough to break a sweat
Baseline to baseline, turn on both feet
bad: Starting hard — this is the raise, not the session

good: Hold the fence and let the leg swing from a tall hip
Build the range over the ten, do not force the first one
bad: Throwing the leg and letting the back arch to get height

good: Sit into the bent hip and keep the other leg straight
Chest tall, push back out through the heel
bad: Letting the knee roll in over the toe

good: Drive the back hip to the floor before you rotate
Reach the top hand at the sky and follow it with your eyes
bad: Rushing the rotation before the hip has opened

good: Tall through the hips, strike the ground underneath you
Quiet, rhythmic contacts
bad: Reaching the foot out in front of the body

good: Bounce off stiff ankles, knees almost locked
Off the ground as fast as you land
bad: Bending the knees and turning it into a squat jump

good: From tall on the toes, snap down into an athletic stance and freeze
Feel your hips go back and your knees bend to soak it up
Land quiet — you should hear almost nothing
bad: Landing stiff-legged and taking it through the knees
Wobbling out of the position instead of sticking it

good: Accelerate hard, then kill it in two steps and hold the stance
Drop the hips on the stop — the last two steps get wider and lower
Own the stop before you make it faster
bad: Slowing down gradually over five or six steps

good: Shuffle 3 m low, plant the outside foot, then sprint 5 m off it
The plant foot lands outside your hip — that is what turns you
Get the shoulders pointing where you are going before the second step
bad: Standing up tall to change direction
Taking a little stutter step before the plant

good: Run 8 m out, plant one foot, turn 180° and sprint 5 m back
Brake over two steps, then push — do not drift the turn wide
Turn off the same foot for a whole set, then swap
bad: Rounding the turn like a running track
Always turning off your strong side and never training the other
